business_rules.name: Authorize access only after successful user validation
business_rules.description: Access control runs in stages: the request proceeds to authorization only after the user-validation step succeeds (via SECMGR). If validation fails, authorization is not attempted.

business_rules.name: Log access only after successful authorization

business_rules.name: Commit to DB2 every 1,000 rows and update the restart checkpoint
business_rules.description: During the history load, the DB2 unit of work is committed whenever the running row counter reaches the commit threshold (1,000 rows), after which the restart checkpoint is updated. This bounds how much any rollback can undo and makes the load restartable.

business_rules.name: Commit when the records-processed count reaches the commit frequency (or is forced)
business_rules.description: The commit controller issues a DB2 COMMIT when the caller's processed-record count reaches the configured commit frequency, or when a force-commit flag is set — letting each caller control its own commit cadence.

condition.text: IF threshold reached OR forced -> commit

business_rules.name: Dispatch checkpoint/restart operation by entry-point code
business_rules.description: The checkpoint service selects its operation from the caller's entry-point code — INIT (initialise), TAKE (take a checkpoint), COMMIT, or RESTART — routing each to its handler.

business_rules.name: Dispatch portfolio maintenance by CRUD command
business_rules.description: The portfolio master service routes each call by its single-letter command: C creates, R reads, U updates and D deletes a portfolio record; any other command is rejected as invalid.

business_rules.name: Dispatch cursor operation by request type
business_rules.description: The cursor manager selects a DB2 cursor lifecycle operation from the request type — Declare, Open, Fetch or Close — so callers drive a cursor through one shared service.

business_rules.name: Dispatch batch-control function by function code
business_rules.description: The batch control processor routes by a four-character function code: INIT initialises a job, CHEK checks prerequisites, UPDT updates status, TERM finalises; any other code is treated as an error.

business_rules.name: Dispatch process-sequence function by function code
business_rules.description: The process sequence manager routes by function code: INIT builds the run sequence, NEXT selects the next ready process (checking its dependencies), STAT refreshes status, TERM computes the final status; any other code is rejected.

business_rules.name: Dispatch DB2 connection function by function code
business_rules.description: The DB2 connection manager routes by function code — CONN connects (with bounded retry), DISC commits and disconnects, STAT checks the live connection; any other code is an error.

business_rules.name: Dispatch DB2 commit-controller function by function code
business_rules.description: The commit controller routes by function code: INIT resets counters, CMIT commits (by frequency or force), RBAK rolls back, SAVE creates a savepoint, REST restores to one, STAT reports counts; any other code is an error.

business_rules.name: Dispatch DB2 error-handler function by function code
business_rules.description: The SQL error handler routes by function code — LOG records the error to the ERRLOG table, DIAG classifies a SQLCODE into a message and severity, RETR fetches the latest logged error; any other code is an error.

business_rules.name: Dispatch DB2 statistics function by function code
business_rules.description: The statistics collector routes by function code: INIT creates the session stats row, UPDT stores current counters, TERM finalises with elapsed/CPU time, DISP displays them; any other code is an error.
